split_questions.question: how does michelin tell if it actually created value in a given year?
split_questions.answer_a:
Michelin says it has **created value during the year** if its **ROCE is greater than the WACC** for that year: “**If ROCE is greater than the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) for the year, then the Group has created value during the period**” ([Michelin-p352-text-1335], “If ROCE is greater than the weighted average cost of capital (WACC)”).

It also explains how ROCE is calculated: it is “**measured by dividing net operating profit after tax (NOPAT) by the average economic assets employed during the year**” ([Michelin-p352-text-1335], “dividing net operating profit after tax (NOPAT) by the average economic assets employed during the year”).

For its 2030 target, Michelin also states it wants to “**Continuously create value between 2023 and 2030, with a more than 10.5% ROCE each year**” ([Michelin-p42-text-101], “more than 10.5% ROCE each year”).
split_questions.answer_b: Michelin tells if it actually created value in a given year by measuring its Total Shareholder Return (TSR), which takes into account changes in the share price as well as dividends received and reinvested. The TSR is calculated using the standard method used by major financial data providers, which considers the annual average of daily closing prices for the year preceding the three-year period under review (including dividends paid in that year) and the annual average of daily closing prices for the last year of the three-year period under review (including dividends paid each year during the period). If Michelin’s TSR was at least 5 points higher than the Stoxx Europe 600 Net Return, the achievement rate would be 100% and the maximum 20% of performance share rights would vest.
